 This Appeal, Coming On For Further Orders, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21.02.2017 passed in MVC No.1486/2014 by the Court of the Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Hassan, (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10.07.2014 at about 4.30 p.m. in front of Anjaneya Temple, Chikkahonnenahally road, the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a bike bearing registration No.KA-13-Y-4780 duly insured with the Insurance Company and the rider of the said motor cycle drove it in a rash and negligent manner and because of which the bike fell down and petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Dislocation of left elbow;
2. Fracture radial head right;
3. Fracture oleron right and 4. Dislocation, tenderness chest;
5. Tenderness TL spine and 6. Abrasion to shoulder.
4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.5,73,489/- along with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization under the following heads:-
Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,07,489/-

account of permanent disability Future medical expenses Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of amenities and life  Rs.30,000/-

 period  TOTAL Rs.5,73,489/-
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident occurred in the year 2014.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.8,500/- per month.
The petitioner was aged 28 years at the time of accident.

Given the age of the petitioner, multiplier of 17 has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has suffered total body disability of 25%.
Thus, towards 'loss of future income' the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.4,33,500/- (Rs.8,500/- x 12 x 17 x 25%) as against Rs.3,06,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

6. In respect of other heads of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, after arguing the matter for sometime, both the learned counsel for appellant as well as respondent No.1-insurance company submit that compensation as awarded by the Tribunal may be retained as the same is just fair and reasonable.
7. Their submission is placed on record.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,27,500/- (Rs.4,33,500 /- minus Rs.3,06,000/-).

Further, given the bank rate of interest, it would be appropriate to award interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. on the enhanced compensation amount from the date of petition before Tribunal till realization.
